newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenspan still throws shadow over German shares.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan still throws shadow over German shares.

text.p: The German share market remained in thrall to Alan Greenspan on Wednesday afternoon, as the Federal Reserve chairman's potentially strongly market moving testimony this afternoon loomed.
The IBIS DAX index, which charts electronic trade in Germany's 30 blue chips, was up 9.03 points at 3,242.37 points at 1324 GMT, after the DAX closed bourse trade at 3,237.87.

"We need him to say something more positive, in fact anything positive at all would help," said a dealer at a major Frankfurt bank of Greenspan's 1500 GMT speech. "The word 'normalisation' is what I'll be looking for."
Greenspan threw global markets into disarray late last year when he warned markets of "irrational exuberance."

And because markets have largely extended their gains since that time, stoping only for a brief retreat, dealers in Frankfurt said there was still a risk that Greenspan could take verbal action once again to halt the advance.
"It's not a day for making bets," another trader said.

The broad market was uneven but the clear outperformer was pharmaceutical company Schering AG, which was up nearly five percent at 153.10 marks in afternoon trade, maintaining gains after a steep early rally.
Schering was boosted from the start by speculation that Japan may be about to remove a ban on the contraceptive pill and by its own forecasts for growth in sales in niche products.
Utility RWE AG got a late boost and was trading up 2.6 percent at 75.95 points in late trade after it reported sales and earnings for 1996/1997, which analysts described as satisfactory overall.
